**Abstract**: A fun two-player minigame for settling conflicts over jousting.

**Proposed name:** Joust\!

**Engine**: Unity 2D

**Inspirations**: Gentlemen’s dispute, I guess

**Art style**: hand-drawn-like

**Structure**: Player-versus-player on a single scene/level, no saving game or online functionalities.

**Gameplay**: Each player takes control of a jousting knight on a horse, equipped with a lance and a shield.  
At each turn, the players can tap a button to accelerate and hold down the right input to make their lance go from vertical down to level, depending on how long they hold down the button.  
The player can use a shield to guarantee survival in that round, but the shield has its own endurance and will get damaged. Hitting the opponent's shield damages your lance and makes it shorter.  
The player can also choose to jump over the opponent, but that comes with a risk of being hit by a somewhat vertical lance.  
Each turn ends with one of the players losing or each player at the opposite side, ready to charge in the other direction.

**Design notes**:

- The damage dealt to the opponent’s shield should be dependent on the velocity gained by tapping the “accelerate” button. ✅  
- Possible addition: Knocking the other player off of their horse might not end the fight; in that case, both players engage in a simple melee (sword) combat.  
- Possible addition: Each fight ends with the camera rotating 180 degrees, showing the reaction of some king to the match's outcome. ✅ almost  
- Possible addition: A bonus setting that enables giving both players randomised upgrades each turn they survive.

**Milestones**:

- Basic gameplay loop, movement, camera-work ✅  
- Polish the combat system ✅ almost  
- Graphics and audio  
- Bonus additions
